question: A 50,000 g cart on a lab bench moves at a speed in m/s equal to the area under y = 2x² + 5x from x = 0 to x = 1. A data logger records its energy of motion. It then applies four corrections in order: it adds 14 J, adds 7 J, subtracts 12 J, and adds 7 J. The bench is 1.8 m long. What is the corrected energy, in J?

A robotics lab's final energy figure, in kJ, is 1 kJ less than a stored-energy figure that is itself expressed in kJ. That stored-energy figure is 19 J more than the combined energy of motion of 8 identical rover wheels. Each wheel has a mass of 6 kg and moves at a speed in m/s equal to the slope of the curve y = 4x³ - 5x² at the point x = 1. What is the lab's final figure, in kJ?

A 61,000 g test block on an industrial shaker table is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under the curve y = 2x² + 3x between x = 1 and x = 4. The force the table must apply to the block is converted to kN. The plant has 9 tables, each carrying 9 such blocks. The engineer therefore multiplies the per-block force by 9 and then by 9 again. What total force does the engineer obtain, in kN?

The total thrust a launch crew records, in N, is 4 times the thrust of a single booster. A single booster supplies exactly the force needed to accelerate a 19,000 g test payload at a certain rate. That rate, in m/s², is obtained by starting from 8 times the sum of 9 and 8, then subtracting 28, then subtracting 13, and finally subtracting 23. What total thrust does the crew record, in N?

The final figure in a foundry's press report, in kN, is 4 times a line total. The line total is 3 times a bay total, and the bay total is 8 times the force of a single ram, expressed in kN. A single ram accelerates a 147 kg die at a rate in m/s² equal to the number of ways to choose 4 items from a set of 8. The press hall is kept at 22 °C. What is the final figure in the report, in kN?

An 84 kg load on a conveyor is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the larger root of x² - 15x + 56 = 0. The force required for this is supplied by each of 11 conveyor drives, and the plant sums the 11 outputs. There are 5 conveyors per line, 3 lines per hall, and 12 halls, so the plant total is that sum multiplied by 5, then by 3, then by 12. Each conveyor belt is 25 m long. What is the plant total, in N?

A 21,000 g electric-scooter test frame is set to a speed in m/s found by taking the larger root of x² - 11x + 24 = 0, multiplying it by 6, and subtracting 26. Its energy of motion at that speed is measured on a bench. Then 19 J of bearing loss is subtracted. The bench repeats the run 9 times and reports the sum, which is 9 times the single-run value. What sum does the bench report, in J?

A 9,000 g package on a sorting chute slides at a speed in m/s equal to the sum of 2k - 1 for k running from 1 to 4. Its energy of motion is converted to kJ. Four packages ride each chute, there are 12 chutes per sorter, and 8 sorters in the depot, so the depot total is the per-package value multiplied by 4, then by 12, then by 8. The chute is 6 m long. What is the depot total, in kJ?

A 104,000 g sled on a rocket-sled track is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to 7 more than the number of ways to choose 2 sensors from a set of 12. The thrust required for this is converted to kN. The track runs 5 sleds per session and 9 sessions per week, so the weekly thrust tally is the single-sled value multiplied by 5 and then by 9. The track is 2 km long. What is the weekly tally, in kN?

A 165 kg forging on a hammer press is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the second derivative of y = 1·x³ + 1·x² evaluated at x = 3. The force required for this is supplied by each of 7 hammers striking together, and the press sums the 7 outputs. The sum is converted to kN. The press hall has 10 presses and the company has 8 such halls, so the company figure is the per-press value multiplied by 10 and then by 8. The forging is heated to 1100 °C before striking. What is the company figure, in kN?

An 80,000 g pallet on a warehouse lift is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 6x between x = 1 and x = 3. The lift motor supplies the force needed for this, less 29 N that a counter-spring contributes. That motor force is converted to kN. A 15 kN safety allowance is then added. What is the resulting figure, in kN?

A 21,000 g payload on a robot arm is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the number of ways to pick 2 grippers from a set of 8. The arm must supply the force for this. A cell has 11 arms and a factory floor has 6 cells, so the floor total is the single-arm force multiplied by 11 and then by 6. From that total, 17 N of cable drag is subtracted, and the result is converted to kN. What is the result, in kN?

A 36,000 g projectile on a pneumatic test cannon is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the sum of 2k - 1 for k from 1 to 7, minus 13. The cannon must supply the force for this. The range has 9 cannons per bay, 9 bays, and runs 2 shifts, so the range total is the single-cannon force multiplied by 9, then by 9, then by 2. Each cannon barrel is 4 m long. What is the range total, in N?

The figure a crane inspector writes down, in kN, is 20 kN of static preload added to a nine-cable total. The nine-cable total is 9 times a single-cable force expressed in kN. The single-cable force is what is needed to accelerate a 136,000 g hook block at a rate in m/s² equal to the larger root of x² - 3x + 2 = 0. What figure does the inspector write down, in kN?

The total a test-track engineer quotes, in kJ, is 7 times a session figure. The session figure is the combined energy of motion of 10 identical test carts, converted to kJ. Each cart has a mass of 36,000 g and moves at a speed in m/s equal to the slope of the curve y = 5x³ - 2x² at the point x = 2. What total does the engineer quote, in kJ?

The total force in a lift-motor report, in N, is 9 times a single-motor figure. The single-motor figure is 6 N less than the force needed to accelerate an 84 kg cabin at a certain rate. That rate, in m/s², is found by taking the second derivative of y = 1·x³ - 5x² at x = 1, multiplying it by 3, and adding 24. What total does the report give, in N?

A rider and bike with a combined mass of 46,000 g move at a speed in m/s equal to 5 times the smaller root of x² - 9x + 18 = 0. The energy of motion is converted to kJ. The ride took 25 minutes. A relay team has 3 such riders, and the club fields 4 teams, so the club figure is the single-rider value multiplied by 3 and then by 4. What is the club figure, in kJ?

A 112 kg sled on a rocket test track is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to 2 times the sum of 7 and 9. The thrust needed for this is reduced by 19 N of aerodynamic assist from a tailwind, then increased by 8 N of rail friction. The track is 1.5 km long. Eleven sleds run in the campaign, so the campaign total is 11 times the single-sled figure. What is the campaign total, in N?

The final entry in a lab logbook, in kJ, is 8 times a per-trial figure. The per-trial figure is 20 J more than the energy of motion of a cart, with the sum then converted to kJ. The cart has a mass of 52 kg and moves at a speed in m/s equal to the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 2x between x = 2 and x = 3. The lab bench is 3 m long. What is the final entry, in kJ?

The total in a drone-motor report, in kN, is 8 times a per-drone figure. The per-drone figure is 2 times a single-motor thrust expressed in kN. A single motor supplies the force needed to accelerate a 3 kg test mass at a rate in m/s² equal to the smaller root of x² - 8x + 15 = 0. What total does the report give, in kN?

A 56 kg cart on a factory test rail moves at a speed in m/s equal to the area under the curve y = 1·x² + 1·x between x = 0 and x = 3. Its energy of motion is reduced by 7 J of bearing loss and then by a further 15 J of air drag. The rail sits at a temperature of 19 °C. There are 8 carts per rail and 8 rails in the hall, so the hall total is the per-cart value multiplied by 8 and then by 8 again. What is the hall total, in J?

A 28,000 g test block on a bench is accelerated at a rate in m/s² equal to the area under y = 1·x² + 7x between x = 1 and x = 2. The force needed for this is converted to kN. The bench log defines a net force as that value minus a 28 kN clamping force plus a 5 kN spring assist, with the driving direction positive, so the net can be negative. The bench is 2.2 m long. Three benches are combined, so the log multiplies the net force by 3. What does the log show, in kN?

The total force a launch crew records, in N, is 11 times a single-booster figure. The single-booster figure is 8 N less than the force needed to accelerate a 55,000 g payload at a certain rate. That rate, in m/s², is the sum of 2k - 1 for k from 1 to 7, minus 5. What total does the crew record, in N?

A 26,000 g projectile leaves a test launcher at a speed in m/s equal to 3 times the sum of 8 and 14. Its energy of motion is converted to kJ, and 28 kJ of launcher recoil loss is subtracted. The launcher barrel is 3 m long. Three launchers fire per volley and 7 volleys are fired, so the total is the per-shot value multiplied by 3 and then by 7. What is the total, in kJ?

A 51,000 g cargo pod on a test sled moves at a speed in m/s equal to the number of ways to choose 2 items from a set of 9. Its energy of motion, less 29 J of runner loss, is converted to kJ. The sled track is 500 m long. Two pods are tested, so the report doubles the per-pod value. What does the report give, in kJ?
